preconditions.description: The input is a string representing the binary tree structure.
The input represents a valid binary tree with 1 to 10^5 nodes, where each node data is between 0 and 10^5.

postconditions.description: The output consists of exactly two lines.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) for x in stdout.strip().splitlines()[0].split())
postconditions.description: The first line contains space-separated integers representing the level order traversal of the tree.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) for x in stdout.strip().splitlines()[1].split())
postconditions.description: The second line contains space-separated integers representing the inorder traversal of the tree.

The underlying tree structure has been modified such that for every node, its nextRight pointer points to the immediate right sibling at the same level, or NULL if it is the rightmost node at that level.
